BSPC_05_2025_Real_time_classification_of.sample_abstract: HONG et al.: REAL-TIME BLOOD PRESSURE CHANGES DETECTION FROM THE PHOTOPLETHYSMOGRAM 1 Using Photoplethysmography to Detect Real-time Blood Pressure Changes with a Calibration-free Deep Learning Model Jingyuan Hong, Manasi Nandi, Weiwei Jin, and Jordi Alastruey Abstract— Blood pressure (BP) changes are linked to individual health status in both clinical and non-clinical settings. This study developed a deep learning model to classify systolic (SBP), diastolic (DBP), and mean (MBP) BP changes using photoplethysmography (PPG) waveforms. Data from the Vital Signs Database (VitalDB) comprising 1,005 ICU patients with synchronized PPG and BP record￾ings was used. BP changes were categorized into three labels: Spike (increase above a threshold), Stable (change within a ± threshold), and Dip (decrease below a thresh￾old). Four time-series classification models were studied: multi-layer perceptron, convolutional neural network, resid￾ual network, and Encoder. A subset of 500 patients was randomly selected for training and validation, ensuring a uniform distribution across BP change labels.
